title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: in the 'équation des lacets' manuscript, Grothendieck studies a profinite group M (apparently related to Ĝ = automorphisms of the profinite π1 of P^1−{0,1,∞}, i.e. the setting of the Grothendieck–Teichmüller group). M contains Π_0 (the profinite fundamental group), a subgroup M(0) and its index-≤2 subgroup M''(0), and M^!_0 := M(0)·Π_0. There is a character ε_2 : M → μ = {±1}. There is a group 𝔖 mapping canonically onto 𝔖_3 (permutations of {0,1,∞}), with induced sign sg : 𝔖 → μ. 𝔖^+ is a subgroup of 𝔖. ρ is the element of order 3 (cyclic permutation) and τ' = τσ an element of order 2. Z_ρ is the centralizer of ρ and N*_ρ = μ_{τ'}·Z_ρ its normalizer. The previous page proves a Lemma from the congruence [x,u] ≡ sg(x)^{ε_2(u)} mod Π_0, valid for x∈𝔖 and u∈M^!. The Lemma says: for x∈𝔖^+ and u∈M^!_0, we have xux^{-1}∈M^!_0 iff sg(x)=1 or ε_2(u)=1.

This page draws consequences.
- Corollary 1: an element x∈𝔖^+ normalizes M^!_0 iff sg(x)=+1.
- Corollary 2: M''^!_0 = M''(0)·Π_0 is normalized by all of 𝔖^+. On M''(0), ε_2 is trivial, so condition (c) of the Lemma holds automatically.
- Since ρ is a 3-cycle, sg(ρ)=+1, so ρ normalizes M^!_0. Hence Z^!_{ρ0} = Z_ρ ∩ M^!_0 = M'(−j) is normal in Z_ρ. Recall Z_ρ = L_ρ·Z^!_ρ, and the remaining generators are handled by ρ.
- Intersecting with M^0(−j)×μ gives that M^0(−j) is normal in Z_ρ. Alternatively, M^0(−j) = Z_ρ ∩ M''^!_0, with M''^!_0 normalized by ρ.
- Conclusion: the four subgroups listed in (39) are all normal in Z_ρ.

Next question: are they normal in N*_ρ = μ_{τ'}·Z_ρ? It suffices to check whether τ' normalizes them.
- This is clear for Z^!_ρ = Z_ρ ∩ M^!, so N^!_ρ = μ_{τ'}·Z^!_ρ is a subgroup of N*_ρ.
- For the other subgroups one must make explicit the action of τ' on Z^!_ρ = M'(−j)×μ.
- The next page does this via τ'(x) ≡ ε_2(x)τ(x) mod Π_0. It finds that only M'(−j) fails to be normal in N*_ρ.

Purpose: determine the normal-subgroup lattice of the centralizer/normalizer of the order-3 torsion element ρ. This is part of analysing torsion and the local structure of the extended Teichmüller/GT-type group near the elliptic point j (the 'lacets' equations at the order-3 point).
errors: Corollary 1's 'il faut' direction tacitly requires the existence of some u∈M^!_0 with ε_2(u)=−1. Since M^!_0 ⊃ M(0) ⊋ M''(0), this presumably holds, but it is not stated.
The reduction to checking [x,u]∈Π_0 for u∈M(0) presupposes that x normalizes Π_0. The previous page mentions this, but it is not re-verified here for elements of 𝔖^+.
No genuine mathematical error is visible. The step 'normal in Z_ρ because normalized by ρ' relies on Z_ρ = L_ρ·Z^!_ρ (asserted as trivial on the previous page).

ideas.what: Criterion for elements of 𝔖^+ to normalize M(0)·Π_0 via the sign character and the commutator congruence [x,u] ≡ sg(x)^{ε_2(u)} mod Π_0
ideas.modern_name: normalizer computation in an extension of 𝔖_3 by an (outer) automorphism group of the profinite free group; sign/ε_2 cocycle
ideas.usually_credited_to: no specific credit; routine within GT-type group theory (cf. later work on torsion in ĜT by Lochak–Schneps)

ideas.what: Normal subgroups of the centralizer Z_ρ of the order-3 element ρ and of its normalizer N*_ρ = μ_{τ'}·Z_ρ; only M'(−j) fails to be normal in N*_ρ
ideas.modern_name: local structure (centralizer/normalizer) of torsion elements in a Teichmüller/GT-type profinite group, at the elliptic point j (order 3)
ideas.usually_credited_to: unsure; related themes appear in Lochak–Schneps and Nakamura on torsion and centralizers in ĜT and profinite mapping class groups
ideas.where_published: La Longue Marche (1981) discusses the Teichmüller tower and torsion elements in general terms; this specific computation is not known to be published

deep.surprise_reason: A routine group-theoretic bookkeeping step (normality of four subgroups in a centralizer and normalizer) inside a long computation. Interesting only as part of Grothendieck's unpublished analysis of torsion in the 'lacets' group, with no standalone new result.
transcription_corrections: 'Ainsi les quatre groupes (3g)' should read '(39)', referring to equation (39), as confirmed by the next page.
'(On encore ; ce groupe est égal' should read '(Ou encore ; ce groupe est égal à Z_ρ∩M''^!_0'.
'Il en est donc de = de l'intersection' should read 'Il en est donc de même de l'intersection'.

'Pour voir ... faut autres sous-groupes' should read approximately 'Pour voir lesquels des autres sous-groupes mentionnés ci-dessus sont normalisés, il faudrait donc expliciter l'action de τ' sur Z^!_ρ = M'(−j)×μ'. The struck text contained 'M^0(−j) = Z_ρ∩M''^!_0, il'.
In Corollary 1: 'il faut et suffit qu'on ait sg(x)=+1' (the [?] is unnecessary).
